summary: If a $CLIP_PENDING_VERIFY clip's sidecar exists but its paired .txt caption is ALSO missing, self_heal.py's --verify-only subprocess call crashes silently inside post_reel.py BEFORE it ever reaches the verify-only branch, because post_reel.py reads --caption-file unconditionally outside any try/except. The resulting behavior is SAFE (never misattributes, never crashes the driver) but only by accident -- via a chain of silent exception-swallowing across two files -- not by designed handling, and this exact scenario has zero test coverage.
description: post_reel.py:87-88 executes `video = os.path.abspath(a.video); assert os.path.exists(video)` and `caption = open(a.caption_file, encoding='utf-8').read().strip()` BEFORE the `try:` at line 90 -- i.e. completely outside all exception handling in main(). If self_heal.py picks a clip whose `.txt` sidecar is missing (its own .mp4 exists, its before-hrefs.json sidecar exists and is valid, but its .txt is gone -- e.g. from a partial manual cleanup), `self_heal.py:_call_verify_only` (lines 47-56) invokes `post_reel.py --verify-only --caption-file <missing .txt path> ...`, which raises an uncaught FileNotFoundError at line 88 and prints NOTHING to stdout. `_call_verify_only`'s own broad `try: d = json.loads(out.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]) if out.stdout.strip() else {} / except Exception: d = {}` (self_heal.py:53-55) receives an empty stdout, sets d={}, and `d.get('ok')` is falsy, so the function returns None. self_heal.py's `_read_fn` (line 76) coerces this via `_call_verify_only(...) or []` to an empty list `[]`. Three consecutive `[]` reads trivially satisfy `_reads_stable([], [])` (set([]) == set([])), so `stabilize_reads` reports stable=True with hrefs=[]. `new_hrefs = [] - set(before_hrefs)` is then empty, so the driver falls into the 'no new href' branch and returns still-pending (self_heal.py:88-91) -- correctly SAFE (never falsely resolves this clip, never duplicate-posts), but this safety is an emergent side-effect of three independent layers of silent exception-swallowing (post_reel.py's uncaught crash producing empty stdout -> self_heal's try/except defaulting to {} -> the trivial empty-list stabilize), not an intentionally-designed handling path. The underlying crash is never logged or surfaced anywhere; a clip stuck in this state will silently repeat this same crash-and-swallow chain on every wake indefinitely with no signal to a human or to monitor.sh that anything is wrong. Neither behavioral-spec.md's REQ-008 nor verification-architecture.md's PROP-006 discuss this specific case (missing .txt alongside a present, valid sidecar) -- only the missing/corrupt SIDECAR case (step 3 / PROP-006(c)) is explicitly designed for and tested.
risk: A future, unrelated change to _call_verify_only's exception handling (e.g. tightening the except clause, or adding stdout validation) could silently remove this accidental safety net with no test to catch the regression -- the clip would then either crash the self-heal driver outright, or (worse) be exposed to whatever `d.get('ok')`/`d.get('reels')` happens to default to.
